claim: Spider 2.0 enterprise databases often exceed 1,000 columns (some over 3,000), and naive LLMs collapse: o1-preview solves only 17.1% and GPT-4o only 10.1% of tasks, versus 86.6% for GPT-4o on Spider 1.0.
quote: databases in Spider 2.0 are sourced from real data applications, often containing over 1,000 columns ... GPT-4o, the success rate is only 10.1% on Spider 2.0 tasks, compared to 86.6% on Spider 1.0

claim: LinkAlign frames schema linking on large multi-database settings as a coarse-to-fine pipeline: multi-round semantic retrieval with query rewriting to find candidate schemas, argmax LLM selection of the target database, then multi-agent debate to extract tables/columns; it reaches 33.09% execution accuracy on Spider 2.0-Lite with open-source LLMs.
quote: Achieves 33.09% execution accuracy on Spider 2.0-Lite benchmark using open-source LLMs—state-of-the-art at submission time.

claim: CRED-SQL's CLSR clusters columns by semantic similarity with K-means and weights rare attributes higher (inverse cluster size), boosting large-DB table recall to 0.40@1 / 0.77@3 on SpiderUnion versus CRUSH's 0.09@1, and lifting end-to-end accuracy to 73.4% (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B), ~22 points over CRUSH.
quote: CLSR achieves 0.40 recall @1 vs. CRUSH's 0.09 ... SpiderUnion: CRED-SQL achieves 73.4% with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B ... Outperforms CRUSH by ~22 percentage points on SpiderUnion

claim: LitE-SQL pre-computes per-column embeddings (column name, description, table name, value description, types, keys, sample values) with a fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B-Embedding model, stores them in ChromaDB, and at inference retrieves top-k=25 columns by cosine similarity, cutting latency to ~25s vs CHESS's ~84s while hitting 72.1% EX on BIRD.
quote: pre-computes schema embeddings ... stored in ChromaDB ... The optimal k-value is empirically set to 25 ... LitE-SQL: 24.979 seconds average inference latency ... CHESS (200B): 83.631 seconds

claim: Schema pruning helps even when models could fit the full schema: with oracle schema, pruning 71.3% of columns raised execution accuracy from 79.3% to 86.3%; small models with <2k-token context windows cannot fit large schemas, motivating splitting schemas into parallel chunks of up to 64 columns, with literal values found by keyword-matching question terms to cell values (top-3 per column).
quote: smaller models usually have shorter context windows (i.e. <2k tokens) ... Full schema: 79.3% ... Pruned schema (71.3% reduction): 86.3% accuracy ... we select values for columns ... by simply matching keywords in questions and values

claim: Fixed top-k retrieval over schema is brittle because too-small k drops needed tables and too-large k injects noise; a RAG architecture with hierarchical clustering can dynamically determine how many relevant schemas to return instead of a static k.
quote: introducing a unique hierarchical clustering mechanism to dynamically determine the number of relevant schemas, minimizing noise ... fixing k can lead to errors where irrelevant tables are included as noise or necessary tables are missing
